healthcareSystem: Dual public-private system. Public healthcare is free for citizens and visitors at point of service. Private clinics offer faster, more comfortable care. Good overall quality for a small island nation.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is decent for an island nation. Public hospitals provide free basic care but can be crowded. Private clinics in Port Louis and tourist areas offer good quality care with shorter waits. English and French-speaking doctors widely available. Complex cases may require transfer to South Africa or India.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 9am-6pm weekdays, 9am-12pm Saturdays. Some pharmacies in tourist areas have extended hours. Hospital pharmacies available 24/7.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are well-stocked with European and Indian-manufactured medications. Pharmacists generally speak English and French. Look for 'Pharmacie' signs. Medications are affordable. Major brands available.
prescriptionRules: Prescription system is enforced for antibiotics and stronger medications. Basic OTC medications readily available. Pharmacists can recommend appropriate medications for minor ailments.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly illegal. Mauritius has very strict drug laws with severe penalties.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances require a doctor's letter and original prescription. Mauritius has strict drug penalties.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry original packaging and prescription documentation.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing medications. English or French documentation accepted. Keep all medications in original packaging. Mauritius has strict drug laws — proper documentation prevents issues at customs.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance recommended especially for water sports and outdoor activities. Ensure coverage includes emergency evacuation to South Africa or India for serious conditions. Diving-specific insurance recommended if scuba diving.

required: Yellow Fever (required if arriving from an endemic country)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow Fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Mauritius is malaria-free. Standard travel vaccinations recommended.

waterNotes: Tap water is generally treated and considered safe in urban areas, but bottled water is recommended for visitors to avoid adjustment issues. Bottled water is widely available and affordable.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety standards are generally good. Street food is popular and usually safe from busy vendors. Seafood is fresh and a highlight — eat at reputable restaurants. Exercise normal caution with raw shellfish. Hotel and resort restaurants maintain high standards.
medicalTourismNote: Mauritius is developing as a medical tourism destination, particularly for cosmetic surgery, dental procedures, and wellness treatments. Several private clinics market to international patients.
metaDescription: Health guide for Mauritius: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, water safety tips, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: City Clinic
hospitals.notes: Modern private hospital with good facilities. English and French-speaking staff. Popular with tourists.

hospitals.name: Wellkin Hospital
hospitals.notes: Newest private hospital on the island. Excellent facilities and modern equipment. International standard care.

hospitals.name: Dr. Jeetoo Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital. Free treatment including for tourists. Can be crowded. Good emergency department.

hospitals.name: Clinic du Nord
hospitals.notes: Private clinic in the main tourist area of Grand Baie. Convenient for north coast hotels and resorts.

dentalCare.availability: Good availability in Port Louis and tourist areas. Many private dental clinics.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care quality is good at private clinics. Many dentists trained in France or India. Affordable compared to Western prices.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Hotels can recommend nearby dentists. Private dental clinics in Grand Baie and Port Louis accept walk-ins for emergencies.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available in Port Louis through private practices.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are available but limited. English and French-speaking therapists can be found in Port Louis. Hotels may be able to recommend practitioners. Telehealth is also an option.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is improving but still inconsistent. Newer resorts tend to have better accessibility features.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Private hospitals have wheelchair access. Public hospitals vary.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public buses are not wheelchair-accessible. Taxis and hotel transfers are the best option. Some resorts offer accessible transport.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Contact resorts in advance about accessibility needs. Beach wheelchairs available at some resorts. Major tourist sites have varying levels of accessibility.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: PCR and rapid testing available at private clinics and hospitals.
covidStatus.notes: COVID restrictions have been fully lifted. Mauritius relies heavily on tourism and has streamlined entry requirements.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private clinics provide detailed English/French invoices. Some clinics can coordinate directly with international insurers. Pay and claim reimbursement for smaller amounts. Keep all receipts and medical records.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private facilities. Public hospital treatment is free. Payment in Mauritian rupee.

medicalEvacuation.secondaryDestination: Reunion Island (France) or New Delhi, India
medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation needed for complex surgeries, major trauma, or specialized care. South Africa is the nearest destination with world-class medical facilities.

drugNameMap.note: Widely available. French brand names common.
